title: Retries that resend an event under a new id
intent: Review the design proposal in `design.md`, which adds retries to the order-event webhook.
statement: I read `design.md`. The retry schedule covers a 31-minute outage, the delivery state is stored before the first attempt, a failed delivery raises an alert, and `replay` covers the rest. The acceptance criteria follow from the proposal. I find no blocking issue and propose adopting the design as written.

problems.summary: every retry gets a new X-Delivery-Id and the subscriber has no way to detect a repeated event, so a timeout after the subscriber processed the event makes it act twice (for example a second receipt email)

locations.anchor: no field for detecting a repeated event
After a timeout, a connection error, or a 5xx response

problems.summary: only a timeout, a connection error, or a 5xx response is retried, so a 4xx such as 429 or 408, a 3xx, or a non-200 2xx response has no retry, failed state, alert, or replay and the delivery is dropped silently

locations.anchor: After a timeout, a connection error, or a 5xx response

problems.summary: every failed delivery raises its own alert and nothing stops sending to a dead subscriber, so one long outage floods the operators with one alert per event

locations.anchor: raise an alert that names the subscriber

problems.summary: the design stores a delivery state without naming its states, the next attempt time, the worker that runs the retries, or how a restart or several instances behave, so pending retries can be lost or sent twice

locations.anchor: Store each event and its delivery state

problems.summary: the replay command and acceptance criterion 3 (exactly as stored) leave open which X-Delivery-Id a replayed delivery carries and what state it has afterwards, so replaying a delivery that the subscriber already processed repeats the event
acceptance criterion 1 only requires that every event reaches the subscriber, so an implementation that sends the same event several times, or loses it on a restart, still passes

locations.anchor: every event of that period reaches it
